chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, who said:
I asked the Shaykh about the Imams, peace be upon them. He said: Whoever denies one of the living ones has indeed denied the departed ones.

key_terms.أَنْكَرَ: denied or rejected the truth or authority of
key_terms.الشَّيْخَ: the Imam being addressed and asked in this report
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams; the divinely appointed leaders from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْأَحْيَاءِ: the living ones; those Imams who were alive at the time
key_terms.الْأَمْوَاتَ: the departed ones; those Imams who had passed away

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kafi say about denying one of the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the indivisible nature of belief in the Imams عليهم السلام. Denial of any one Imam, especially among the living Imams, is presented as denial of the entire line of Imamate and its divine authority.
